correctness.rationale: Writing s=x(1-x), q=(1-r)/r, lambda=ac/eps, H=q(r)^lambda/s^a+(ak/eps)integral_{1/2}^r q(v)^lambda/(1-v)dv gives H_x xdot+H_r rdot=0 identically. The Hessian at the interior equilibrium (1/2,r*) is positive definite, so by the Morse lemma sufficiently close regular levels form a period annulus with nonzero velocity. Exact time-average of d/dt log(r/(1-r)) yields mean x=1/2; averaging primitive with F'(x)=1/[x(1-x)A(x)] yields mean r=c mean1/A(x). Strict (1-4y^2)^(-a)>1+4a y^2 and nonconstant orbit give variance bound, and uniform small-orbit Taylor gives sharp coefficient. Cauchy--Schwarz proves negative covariance between A(x) and r.
residual_risks: The center is local: no claim of global annulus to the boundary or stability under unbalanced perturbations.
The sharp coefficient is an asymptotic small-orbit infimum, never equality on a finite-amplitude orbit.
